hooks.prompt: PLANE TOOL CALL CHECK. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS. Read `tool_name` and `tool_input.action`. Plane MCP 0.3+ resource tools (workitem, cycle, module, page, ...) take an `action` parameter; older per-operation connectors have no `action` and put the operation in the tool name (delete_cycle, delete_work_item, ...). (1) DESTRUCTIVE: `action` is `delete`, `remove_projects`, `remove_page`, `remove_member`, `detach`, `detach_from_workitem`, `delete_point`, `delete_option`, `delete_value` or `delete_definition`, or the tool name is a legacy `delete_*`. Block the call (ok=false) with a reason that tells Claude to get explicit user confirmation first: (a) show the user the exact resource being deleted (name, ID, a one-line description of what it contains); (b) state what will be lost and what will only be unlinked, e.g. deleting a cycle unlinks its work items but keeps them, deleting a project is catastrophic, deleting a state requires migrating its items first, a page can be deleted only after it is archived; (c) ask 'Proceed with the delete? (yes/no)' and WAIT for 'yes'. If the user says no or is ambiguous, abort and offer a safer alternative (archive instead of delete, migrate the state first). Each destructive call needs its own confirmation, even if the user approved a related one earlier. (2) ARCHIVE: `action` is `archive` (or a legacy archive_*). Allow (ok=true) but warn in one line what gets archived and that `unarchive` reverses it; note that `cycle archive` ends a still-running cycle first and `workitem archive` accepts only completed or cancelled items. (3) Anything else (list, retrieve, create, update, search, count, complete, manage_*, transfer_workitems, ...): allow (ok=true) silently, with no questions. If the tool does not belong to a Plane server, allow it.
